processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: The experimental steel was melted and cast in a 50 kg vacuum induction furnace and then air cooled to RT.
The ingot was reheated to 1250 °C and held for 2 h for homogenization.
The ingot was forged into round bars with a diameter of 60 mm; the starting and finishing forging temperatures were 1100 and 950 °C, respectively.
Followed by cooling to RT in the furnace (furnace cooled).

structures.overall_structure: Initial as-forged microstructure consists of equiaxed grains with a fully austenitic (single-phase fcc) constituent; EBSD phase map shows a single indexed phase and XRD shows only γ reflections.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Density estimated by Kim et al. equation (1) and measured experimentally.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: Apreo S HiVac scanning electron microscope (SEM)
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: EBSD step size 0.5 µm (for deformed-microstructure analyses); initial IPF and phase maps with 50 µm scale bars
characterization_methods.purpose: Analyze the initial microstructure (IPF map) and phase constitution (phase map) of the as-forged steel
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fully indexed, equiaxed austenite grain structure (≈10-50 µm); phase map shows a single indexed phase (fully austenitic), no second phase

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: SmartLab SE X-ray diffractometer with Cu Kα radiation (λ = 0.154060 nm)
characterization_methods.purpose: Confirm the phase constitution of the initial steel and check for isothermal martensite after holding at -196 °C
characterization_methods.key_findings: Only four γ reflections present: γ(111) (~43°), γ(200) (~50°), γ(220) (~74°), γ(311) (~90°); no extra peaks, confirming fully austenitic structure with no isothermal martensite formed at -196 °C

computational_details.simulation_method: Thermodynamic (subregular-solution) calculation of stacking fault energy (SFE)
computational_details.potential_model_or_database: Thermodynamic parameter expressions/values of Ref. [6] (Table 1): ΔG_i^(γ→ε) terms in T, X_Mn, X_C
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: SFE values (32, 40, 61 mJ/m2 for -196 °C, -77 °C and RT) are used to rationalize the observed deformation mechanisms (mechanical twinning at -196 °C, planar glide/microbands elsewhere)

analytical_models.model_note: ΔG^(γ→ε) computed via equation (4) summing elemental and interaction free-energy terms and the FeMnAl/C term; a_γ = 0.36757 nm from XRD.

computational_details.simulation_method: Empirical density estimation from chemical composition
computational_details.validation_against_experiment: Estimated density 7.078 g/cm3 vs measured 7.114 g/cm3

unmapped_findings: The initial as-forged steel is fully austenitic (single phase); no isothermal martensite forms after holding at -196 °C for 30 min, indicating a very stable austenite (XRD only shows γ reflections).
The austenite lattice parameter a_γ was calculated to be 0.36757 nm based on XRD analysis.
The density of the experimental as-forged steel estimated by the Kim et al. equation is 7.078 g/cm3 while the measured density is 7.114 g/cm3.
A representative sample of the as-forged steel was held in liquid nitrogen for 30 min and then analyzed by XRD (low-temperature holding specimen derived from this as-forged steel).

The as-forged state is the common precursor (基态/初始状态) for the subsequent tensile specimens (tested at -196 °C, -77 °C and RT), Charpy impact specimens (tested at -196 °C, -77 °C and RT) and the low-temperature-holding specimen; those deformed/tested states are treated as separate specimens and their data are not attributed to this as-forged sample.
